title: Assessing Future Climate Changes in the East Asian Summer and Winter Monsoon Using Regional Spectral Model

venue.name: Journal of the Meteorological Society of Japan Ser II

abstract: This study investigated potential future climate changes over East Asia with a focus on temperature variation and changes in precipitation as well as future changes in the East Asian monsoon system. The current and future climate projection scenarios are downscaled over East Asia using the regional spectral model (RSM). The representative concentration pathways (RCPs) 2.6 and 8.5 scenarios driven by the Hadley Center Global Environmental Model version 2 (HG2) are used to provide large-scale forcing for the RSM downscaling simulations. Simulations were conducted for the current climate from 1980 to 2005 and two types of future climate between 2020 and 2100. Near-future (2025-2050) and far-future (2075-2100) climate simulations are compared with the current (1980-2005) climatology to investigate climatic change over East Asia. The RSM well captures the precipitation and temperature distribution related to the East Asian summer and winter monsoon and mesoscale mountain range with added values, although the wet and cold biases are aggravated in the RSM downscaling. Additionally, short time-scale phenomena such as daily mean temperature and daily precipitation are more accurately reproduced by the RSM than by the HG2. From future climate projection, the increasing temperature trends of each RCP scenario are consistently reproduced in the RSM downscaling; in particular, the result from the RCP 8.5 experiment shows a significantly steeper trend with increasing temperature. Meanwhile, the East Asian monsoon is intensified in the future climate projection by the strengthening North Pacific subtropical high and Okhotsk high in summer and intensified Siberian high in winter. These changes lead to an increase in precipitation for summer and a decrease for winter.
problem: Coarse spatial resolution in Global Climate Models (GCMs) prevents them from adequately resolving the regional details and mesoscale disturbances essential for accurately simulating future climate changes in the complex East Asian monsoon system, necessitating the use of downscaling with regional models.
method: This study assesses future East Asian climate change by dynamically downscaling global climate model projections under RCP 2.6 and 8.5 scenarios using the Regional Spectral Model, comparing near- and far-future simulations with the current climate to analyze changes in temperature, precipitation, and the monsoon system.
task: The task is to assess future changes in temperature, precipitation, and the monsoon system over East Asia by dynamically downscaling global climate model projections using a regional spectral model.

innovation: This study uses a regional spectral model to project future climate change in East Asia, finding that both the summer and winter monsoons will intensify, leading to increased precipitation in the summer and a decrease in the winter.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: The RSM is applied as a RCM for dynamical downscaling in this study. This model has been extensively used for dynamical downscaling and operational short-range forecasting.
Current and RCP simulations of the Atmosphere-Ocean-coupled Hadley Center Global Environmental Model version 2 (HadGEM2-AO; Baek et al. 2013) are used as large-scale forcing conditions.

The boundary condition is used from the historical run of the HadGEM2-AO (hereafter, called the “HG2”) simulation of National Institute of Meteorological Research of Korea Meteorological Administration (Baek et al. 2013). The HadGEM2-AO (HG2) is composed of an atmospheric GCM with N96 (1.875° × 1.25°) horizontal and 38 vertical levels, 38 km of top altitude, and an ocean GCM with 1° horizontal and 40 vertical levels.

The physics package of the RSM employs the simplified Arakawa-Schubert convection scheme (Hong and Pan 1998) for convective parameterization, a diagnostic microphysics scheme (Hong et al. 1998), a nonlocal boundary layer scheme (Hong and Pan 1996), the National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP)–Oregon State University-U.S. Air Force-National Weather Service Office of Hydrologic Development (NOAH) land surface model (LSM) (Chen and Dudhia 2001; Ek et al. 2003), and short-wave (Chou 1992) and long-wave (Chou et al. 1999) radiation parameterizations.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: To prevent distortion of large-scale fields, the revised scale selective bias correction method is applied, which has contributed to enhance performance of the precipitation simulation in RCM downscaling (Hong and Chang 2012).
The number of grid points in Cartesian coordinates is 200 (west-east) by 165 (north-south), with nominal horizontal resolution of 50 km. A 28-level terrain-following (sigma) vertical grid is used.
